title: Three Years and One Short Clock
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：minute　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 minute 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1988 the keeper ① counted the minute that no traveller in the tower would have counted, and he said the counting was the whole of the year. The ② minute, meaning the moment itself and not the clock, ran three years and stayed uncounted in the book; a minute, he said, is the only thing in a tower that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ minute in that tower had the same short clock beside it, and the ④ minute at the far stair, meaning the bell they kept for the children to ring and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A minute, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the keeper said the counting is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the minute was the whole of the matter, meaning the time and not the moment. The ⑥ minute, meaning the time and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; minute, he said, is either something you count or the only word that means both a moment and a time. He said the time is the part they remember.

By 1993 the ⑦ minute had become a line in a calendar, and the calendar had become an argument about the short clock. The ⑧ minute of the whole thing, the keeper wrote in January, was one tower and three years of counting; minute, he said, is either the bell at the far stair or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ minute I remember is the moment counted in the calendar, which closed in 1995 and is still counted as the quietest in the tower. A ⑩ minute, my mother said in 1997, is the only moment that improves by being counted; every minute, she said, is a time that has agreed to look like a moment. She said the time was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 分钟（指钟楼里每一分旁边的那一分）
B. n. 分钟（指那分分钟本身，与小小的座钟相对）
C. 固定搭配：count the minute 数这一分分钟
D. n. 分钟（指留给孩子们敲的那一口）
E. n. 分钟之事（抽象总称，指一处钟楼的分钟之事）
F. n. 分钟（指年历里写到、被清点的那一分）
G. n. 分钟、光阴（指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 光阴（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: count the minute 意为“数这一分分钟”，1988 年那位守夜人把钟楼里没有一位过路人肯清点的一分分钟做了一遍。
minute 意为“分钟”，指那分分钟本身而不是小小的座钟，它经过了三个年头而在簿子上没有被清点。
minute 意为“分钟”，指钟楼里每一分旁边的那一分，每一分旁边都有同一座小小的座钟。
minute 意为“分钟”，指最远那道旋梯的留给孩子们敲的那一口，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
minute 意为“分钟、光阴”，指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这分光阴就是那件事的全部。
minute 意为“光阴”，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西而不是那分分钟，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
minute 意为“分钟”，指年历里写到、被清点的那一分，到 1993 年这一分成了年历里的一行。
minute 意为“分钟之事”，守夜人一月写道，整件事的分钟之事是一处钟楼和三个年头的清点。
minute 意为“分钟”，我记得的是年历里清点过的那一分，1995 年走完了，至今仍被说成钟楼里最安静的一分。
minute 为抽象总称，母亲 1997 年说，分钟是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的分钟。
